title: Product Photography for South Carolina Businesses
metaTitle: Product Photography for South Carolina Brands | TDM
metaDescription: Product photography for South Carolina brands and suppliers: catalog, lifestyle and detail shots. Shot by TDM's US-based team and retouched for every channel.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) photographs products for South Carolina businesses: clean catalog images, styled lifestyle scenes and close-up detail shots, retouched and delivered in every size your store, marketplace listings and ads require. Our team in the United States photographs the products, in a studio setup or on location depending on what the images need. The files then go to TDM's operations office in Lahore for retouching and export. You approve the shot list and art direction before the shoot and review the results online.

sections.heading: Who needs product photography in this state
paragraphs: Two quite different groups. The first is consumer brands: food and pantry goods, clothing and accessories, candles and skincare, home goods, golf and outdoor products. Many started in Charleston, Greenville or a small town in between, sell on their own Shopify store and on Amazon, and are still using photos taken on a kitchen counter. Those images cost sales, because online the picture is the only way a buyer can inspect the product.

The second group is industrial. The Upstate is full of companies that make components, tools, fittings and packaging for larger manufacturers. Their catalogs often show grey parts on grey benches, or a supplier's drawing. Consistent, well-lit part photography makes a catalog easier to buy from and makes a small supplier look like a serious one to a purchasing team.

sections.heading: How it works from South Carolina
paragraphs: The process starts with a plan, because a shoot moves quickly when every angle has been agreed and slowly when it has not. The same steps apply to a handful of new items and to a whole range.
bullets: Shot list and art direction: we map your catalog, channels and gaps, and agree the angles, scenes and detail shots per product.
Our US-based team photographs the products, in a controlled setup or on location where the setting matters.
The shoot follows the approved list, with lighting and styling kept consistent across the range.
Selected images are retouched at our operations office in Lahore and sent for review, and your revision notes are applied.
Finals are exported in each crop and resolution you need, organised and named to your convention.

sections.heading: What you can ask for
paragraphs: Studio catalog photography on white or coloured backgrounds gives a large range the repeatable look it needs. Sets can be specified to meet Amazon and other marketplace requirements for background, framing and resolution. Lifestyle scenes stage the product with props and surfaces that match your brand, for ads and social posts. Macro shots show materials, finishes, labels and mechanisms, the close views that stand in for holding the item.
Retouching is done for accuracy as well as polish. Colours should match the real product, because misleading images come back as returns.

sections.heading: Studio setup or real location
paragraphs: The first decision is where each image should be made. Catalog and marketplace images need controlled light and a plain background, so they are shot in a studio setup. A photograph that depends on a real South Carolina setting, such as a product on a Lowcountry dock or in a restaurant dining room, is a location shoot, and our US-based team plans it as one. Styled scenes can suggest a setting, but they should not pretend to be a place. Tell us early about perishable food, very heavy or oversized items and one-off pieces you cannot spare for long, because they change how the day is scheduled. Industrial parts raise their own questions: reflective metal, dark rubber and very small components each need different lighting, and it is worth approving a sample image per category before the full range is shot.

faqs.q: Who photographs the products, and where?
faqs.a: TDM's own team in the United States photographs them, in a studio setup or on location depending on the brief. A member of our team is based in South Carolina. Retouching and file preparation are done at our operations office in Lahore, and you review the images online.

faqs.q: How much does product photography cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of products, the number of images per product and how much styling is involved. We quote after a free consultation, once we have seen the range.

faqs.q: How long does a product shoot take?
faqs.a: It depends on the brief, the size of the range and how much styling and retouching the images need. Dates are agreed in the plan before the shoot, so tell us about any launch you are working towards.

faqs.q: Can you photograph a whole catalog, including industrial parts?
faqs.a: Yes. Catalog work is a core part of the service. We set up a repeatable lighting and framing system per category so a large number of items come out consistent, then batch the shooting and retouching.
